reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend with a holidays argument and adds one shared isNonWorkingDay predicate that replaces every isWeekend check, so all paths keep using the shared helpers.

duplication.why: Adds no new copies, but threads holidays separately into blocks the tree already duplicated (the two identical adjust expressions in schedule-template, the two filters in getNextDate, the daily-drop checks in getUpcomingDates/getDatesInRange) instead of consolidating them.

placement.why: The holiday rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to the weekend rule it generalises; call sites only pass their config's holidays.

scope.why: Only the type, the recur-data mapping, the shared helpers, their call sites and a release note change.

maintainability.why: A single predicate defines non-working days, which is easy to extend; the holidays argument has to be remembered at eight call sites and the search margin heuristic (3 + holidays.length) is ad hoc.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every weekend check and move now goes through isNonWorkingDay / getDateWithSkippedWeekend.

disguised_duplication.where: No duplicated logic is introduced or reshaped; existing parallel copies are edited in the same way.

one_place.where: isNonWorkingDay in shared/schedules.ts defines weekend-or-holiday and is used by getDateWithSkippedWeekend, getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template.
